messages:
sam_customer: Hey team — during our sandbox onboarding my app started getting intermittent 503s and a couple 403s when calling the SDK. Started after we switched to the corp proxy. Logs attached below.

sam_customer: snippet: 
```
ERROR 2026-03-18T15:02:01Z request failed status=503 endpoint=https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/chat
CausedBy: TLS handshake error: handshake failure (no SNI)
```

alyssa_cs: thanks for reporting, sam. can you confirm if the requests go through a corporate HTTPS proxy that rewrites SNI or terminates TLS? sounds like SNI/hostname mismatch. :thinking_face:

sam_customer: yes — corporate proxy and they do SSL interception. we did a quick capture and saw the Host header still set to api.redwood.example.com but the TLS SNI is the proxy hostname. not sure how the SDK handles that.

mike_sdk: hmm — our SDK relies on SNI for routing at edge (some customers use SNI routing to pick region). if proxy replaces SNI, edge rejects the handshake -> 503 or 403 depending on policy.

jordan_infra: dovetailing: if the proxy terminates TLS and re-issues client certs, the edge sees unexpected CN/SAN. two mitigation paths: 1) configure proxy to passthrough SNI (preferred) or 2) set an SNI override header in the client so the edge sees the expected name.

alyssa_cs: mike — do we have an env var or config that lets the SDK send a TLS SNI override or force hostname pin?

mike_sdk: we don't expose raw TLS knobs in the high-level SDK, but we do have two supported workarounds: 1) use the HTTP proxy mode that does CONNECT tunneling (preserves SNI), or 2) set REDWOOD_EDGE_HOST to the proxy-resolvable hostname and use our host header override: set REDWOOD_HOST_HEADER=api.redwood.example.com. example: 
```
export HTTP_PROXY=http://corp-proxy:3128
export REDWOOD_HOST_HEADER=api.redwood.example.com
# SDK will open CONNECT -> preserves original TLS to edge
```
Note: CONNECT is best because it preserves TLS end-to-end.

sam_customer: ok will try CONNECT. quick question — we also saw spikes in 429s when we rotated ephemeral tokens; looks like many clients re-auth simultaneously. could that be related?

alyssa_cs: yes, correlated. when token refreshes fan out, proxy+edge sees a spike of new sessions which can push rate limits. how are you rotating tokens?

sam_customer: every worker polls for new token on startup, then refreshes on expiry independently. dozens of workers start at same time during deploy.

mike_sdk: recommended pattern: centralize token refresh or jitter the refresh schedule. token-cache with exponential backoff on 429. pseudocode: 
```
if token_expiring_soon:
  attempt_refresh_with_jitter()
  if 429: backoff_exp_backoff()
```
Also add client-side reuse (in-memory TTL) so not every process fetches a new token simultaneously.

jordan_infra: from infra side we can temporarily raise soft burst window for your account in sandbox to avoid immediate 429s while you switch to buffered refresh. ping me if you want that toggle.

sam_customer: trying CONNECT mode now. will also add jitter + in-memory token cache. thanks everyone. putting the proxy team on slack thread. cc @proxy-team. :thumbsup:

sam_customer: Quick update — switching to CONNECT fixed the handshake errors (no more TLS SNI failures). 429s reduced after adding jittered refresh. marking this resolved for now. Thanks! :tada:
